newsitem.title: UK: London gold mostly steady, silver probes lower.
newsitem.headline: London gold mostly steady, silver probes lower.

text.p: Gold prices oscillated within a narrow price range on Thursday, while silver flirted with downside, testing key support at $5.00 an ounce.
Gold was fixed slightly lower at $382.75 an ounce compared to $383.10 in the morning and $383 on Wednesday afternoon.
Bids were quoted between $383.40 and $382.60, holding reasonably steady above the nearby $382.00 support level.
Dealers said bullion might probe lower, although the downside although looked limited for now.
Silver and the other white metals, however, lost some steam in the afternoon and hovered around key support levels.
Silver was indicated at $4.98/$5.00, down 10 cents from Thursday's London close. If it convincingly broke below support, the next level to watch was $4.93, dealers said.
Comex December silver was down 7.3 cents at $5.025 an ounce.
Palladium, which fell to three-year lows earlier this week, was also probing its key support at $120, dipping to a low bid so far of $119.25 an ounce.
Below $120, palladium was vulnerable to further drops to as low as $112-$115 before finding important support, dealers said.
Platinum was also off the day's highs, indicated down $1.00 at $389.00/$390.00.
Fund and trade buying had raised platinum above $390 on Wednesday. But the move higher was undercut by weakness in silver and a dearth of follow-through interest, dealers said.
Some analysts were concerned that weakness in silver and platinum might undermine a recovery in the gold price.
"Silver at around $5.00 and platinum at $390 makes many people very nervous," one analyst said.

"Expectations for gold to move higher in a better demand environment depend on the behaviour or silver and platinum," he added, emphasising that falls in either of these metals could erode gold's upward potential.
Several analysts and dealers have forecast a short-covering bounce for gold despite uncertainty over whether the International Monetary Fund will decide to sell gold reserves.
But gold still had some room to go a bit lower, they said.
"There's still room to the downside, but not that much," one dealer said, adding that gold may test the nearby $382 support before attempting to bounce higher.
Gold demand is expected to reach its peak from September to March due to Christmas buying in the west and the wedding and festival season in Asia.
